one_line_idea: A paired same-image comparison protocol for detectors, using per-image score differences with sign-flip permutation tests, shrinks comparison uncertainty enough to change published accept/reject conclusions at fixed test-set size.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Detector comparisons report unpaired AP deltas on a shared test set, and small claimed gains (under 0.5 AP) are routinely accepted without any variance accounting.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because per-image difficulty is the dominant variance component and is shared between models evaluated on the same images, a paired design that tests the distribution of per-image metric differences removes that shared component and yields far tighter confidence intervals than image-level bootstrap of each model separately.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On COCO val2017, paired sign-flip confidence intervals for AP-proxy differences between five nearby public detector pairs will be at least 2x narrower than unpaired bootstrap intervals, and at least one of the five pairs will flip between significant and not-significant relative to the unpaired protocol; kill the idea if the average interval-width ratio is under 1.3x or if zero of five pairs change status.
why_important: This is a direct debunk-to-repair conversion: instead of another audit showing detection deltas are noise, it ships a drop-in comparison protocol that makes small-margin conclusions defensible without collecting new data.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Paired tests are standard in ML broadly, but a pre-registered paired-permutation protocol for COCO-style AP with a measured interval-shrinkage factor and conclusion-flip audit appears unpublished for detection.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Evaluate 10 public detectors on COCO val2017, compute per-image matched-detection quality scores, then compare paired sign-flip intervals against unpaired bootstrap intervals for all 45 pairs and count status flips among the 5 closest pairs.
main_risk: AP is a set-level statistic that does not decompose exactly into per-image contributions, so the paired proxy may rank models slightly differently than corpus-level AP and the repair could be rejected on fidelity grounds.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Practitioners treat the shared test set as already controlling for difficulty and assume reported AP deltas are comparable without explicit pairing.
why_it_might_be_wrong: If between-image variance is small relative to within-image matching noise, pairing buys little and interval widths will barely change.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Inference of 10 MMDetection model-zoo checkpoints (e.g., Faster R-CNN, RetinaNet, DETR, YOLOX variants) on COCO val2017 plus permutation statistics runs in under 8 hours on one consumer GPU; all data and models public.

why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Seed-variance complaints exist for detection, but a packaged MDD certificate with hierarchical decomposition over image sampling and seeds, plus a retroactive reclassification audit, appears missing.

one_line_idea: Cryptographic canary items for vision benchmarks: seeding test sets with arbitrary-labeled canary images gives benchmark hosts a statistically powered detector of training-on-test contamination that works as a protocol, not a forensic investigation.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Benchmark hosts cannot verify whether submitted models trained on test data; current contamination arguments rely on circumstantial evidence assembled long after the fact.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Because canary labels are arbitrary (assigned by a keyed rule, not visual content), any above-chance canary accuracy is attributable to test-set exposure, so a small canary set embedded at benchmark creation yields a contamination test with quantifiable power and false-positive control, independent of model internals.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] With 200 canaries embedded in a benchmark, a model finetuned on a training set contaminated with the labeled test data will be detected at over 95% power at a 1% false-positive rate, while clean-trained models of any strength stay at chance on canaries; kill the idea if strong clean models exceed chance on canaries (visual-similarity leakage breaks arbitrariness) or if detection power at 200 canaries falls below 60%.
why_important: This is protocol-level infrastructure: it converts contamination disputes into a routine statistical check that benchmark hosts run at submission time, complementing mechanism-focused memorization research without overlapping it.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Canary strings are established for language-model privacy auditing; a benchmark-side canary protocol for vision test-set contamination with power analysis appears undeveloped.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct a benchmark from ImageNet-subset classes plus 200 keyed-label canaries, finetune ViT-B and ResNet-50 (timm) under clean and deliberately contaminated regimes at several contamination fractions, and trace detection power versus canary count.
main_risk: Sophisticated contamination (training on test images without labels, or on near-duplicates) would evade label-keyed canaries, limiting the protocol to the crudest contamination mode.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Contamination policing is assumed to require either data-pipeline transparency or post-hoc similarity forensics, both impractical at scale.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Public leaderboards may face mostly unlabeled-image contamination, for which this protocol is blind by design, making its deterrence value marginal.
fastest_falsification_experiment: A dozen short finetunes of timm ViT-B/ResNet-50 on ImageNet-100-scale subsets with injected canaries run in about 2 days total on one A100; all components public or scripted.

family_fingerprint.manipulated_variable: keyed canary embedding vs no canaries under controlled contamination

one_line_idea: Noise-ceiling-normalized leaderboards: estimating each benchmark's inter-annotator ceiling and reporting scores as fractions of remaining headroom changes which improvements look meaningful, especially near saturation.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Leaderboards report raw scores with no reference to the benchmark's annotation-noise ceiling, so a 0.5-point gain reads the same at 60% and at 95% of the achievable maximum.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Inter-annotator agreement data (double-annotated subsets that several public datasets already ship) supports estimating a per-benchmark, per-class noise ceiling, and headroom-normalized reporting reorders both class-level priorities and model-level conclusions in the saturation regime.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Using public double-annotation subsets to estimate ceilings on Cityscapes and LVIS, at least 20% of classes will show current best models within measurement noise of the ceiling (making further class gains unmeasurable), and headroom-normalized ranking will flip at least 1 of the top-3 model orderings on one benchmark; kill the idea if estimated ceilings exceed raw best scores by more than 10 points everywhere, meaning saturation is nowhere near and normalization changes nothing.
why_important: Prevents the community from spending compute on classes and benchmarks that are already measurement-limited and redirects it to real headroom, as a reporting capability rather than a critique.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Noise ceilings are standard in neuroscience model evaluation; systematic ceiling-normalized reporting for vision benchmarks appears absent.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Estimate per-class ceilings from annotator-pair agreement on the double-annotated subsets, propagate uncertainty, and re-render public leaderboard slices (top-10 checkpoints) in headroom units with flip analysis.
main_risk: Double-annotated subsets are small and possibly unrepresentative, giving ceiling estimates with error bars wide enough to swallow the conclusions.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Raw metric points are treated as having constant meaning across the score range, and saturation talk stays qualitative.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Model errors and annotator disagreements may be qualitatively different, so agreement-based estimates may not bound achievable model scores in either direction.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Ceiling estimation from public agreement subsets plus re-scoring 10 public checkpoints (MMSegmentation for Cityscapes, MMDetection for LVIS) is inference-plus-analysis, about 1 day on one GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Difficulty-matched test refresh: replacing stale test images with fresh ones matched on anchor-model difficulty profiles preserves model rankings while breaking URL-level and hash-level contamination, enabling routine benchmark rotation.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Benchmarks cannot rotate their test sets without breaking comparability, because fresh images shift difficulty and invalidate historical numbers, so test sets stay static and contaminable for a decade.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] An image's difficulty profile (per-anchor-model scores across a frozen anchor ensemble) is a sufficient statistic for its effect on rankings, so sampling fresh images to match the joint difficulty-profile distribution of retired images yields a replacement set on which rankings and score levels are preserved for non-anchor models.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Swapping 50% of a COCO-classes evaluation set with difficulty-matched fresh images drawn from Open Images will preserve the ranking of 10 held-out public detectors with Kendall tau at least 0.9 and mean absolute score shift under 0.5 AP, versus tau under 0.8 for unmatched refresh; kill the idea if matched refresh does no better than unmatched or tau falls below 0.7.
why_important: Routine rotation is the strongest structural defense against test-set contamination and overfitting, and difficulty matching is the missing piece that keeps longitudinal comparability.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Difficulty estimation per item exists; using anchor-profile matching to certify ranking-preserving test refresh appears untested.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Score anchor and held-out detector pools on COCO val2017 and a relabeled Open Images candidate pool, run matched and random 50% swaps, and compare ranking preservation and score-level drift across 20 refresh replicates.
main_risk: Cross-dataset label-convention differences between the source and refresh pools could dominate the swap effect, confounding the difficulty-matching evaluation.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Test sets are treated as irreplaceable artifacts whose rotation necessarily resets all historical comparisons.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Difficulty profiles from anchors may not span the factors that differentiate future models, so preservation for today's held-out pool may not extend to tomorrow's architectures.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Inference of ~16 public MMDetection checkpoints on COCO val2017 and an Open Images subset with shared classes takes about 1 day on one GPU; both datasets and all models public.

one_line_idea: Partial-pooling estimators for rare-class metrics: hierarchical shrinkage of per-class AP/IoU stabilizes long-tail leaderboards, halving bootstrap rank volatility and changing which long-tail methods win.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Rare-class metrics on long-tail benchmarks rest on a handful of instances per class, so per-class scores and the rare-split averages built from them are wildly unstable, yet leaderboards report them as point values.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Per-class scores share structure (class prototypes, frequency bands), so an empirical-Bayes partial-pooling estimator borrows strength across classes to produce rare-split estimates that are both lower-variance and better predictors of scores on a second sample, changing method comparisons that currently hinge on noise.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On LVIS v1 val, partial-pooled rare-class AP will reduce bootstrap rank volatility among 6 public long-tail methods by at least a factor of 2 and will flip at least 1 published pairwise ordering; cross-validated prediction of held-out-split class scores will improve (lower MSE) for at least 80% of rare classes; kill the idea if volatility reduction is under 1.2x or held-out prediction does not improve.
why_important: Long-tail research currently optimizes against noise on the rare split; a stabilized estimator redirects the subfield toward real effects and is adoptable by the benchmark host directly.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Empirical-Bayes shrinkage is classical; its application to long-tail vision leaderboards with a rank-stability and flip audit appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Fit hierarchical models over per-class AP of 6 public LVIS checkpoints, compare raw vs pooled estimates under bootstrap resampling and split-half validation, and audit ordering flips on the rare split.
main_risk: Shrinkage pulls genuinely exceptional per-class performances toward the mean, and methods specializing on a few rare classes would be systematically under-credited.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Per-class point estimates are treated as the honest raw data, with shrinkage viewed as statistical tampering.
why_it_might_be_wrong: If method effects on rare classes are strongly class-idiosyncratic, no pooling structure fits and the estimator's cross-validation advantage disappears.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Scoring 6 public LVIS checkpoints (MMDetection configs and the public Detic release) plus hierarchical fitting runs in about 8 hours on one GPU; all public.

one_line_idea: Boundary-affinity point supervision: growing instance masks from a 10-click-per-image budget through an affinity field trained only on click pairs reaches most of full-mask panoptic quality, because clicks constrain topology while affinities carry geometry.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Full mask annotation costs about two orders of magnitude more than point clicks, yet point-supervised panoptic pipelines still trail full supervision by a wide margin.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The residual gap is not information-theoretic but architectural: clicks uniquely identify instances (topology) while modern self-supervised features already encode boundary geometry, so a pairwise affinity head trained on click co-membership, decoded with a graph partitioner, converts 10 clicks into masks that capture most of what polygons supply.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On COCO panoptic with 10 simulated clicks per image, affinity-grown supervision will reach at least 88% of the full-mask-trained PQ of the same architecture, and at least +4 PQ over strongest point-loss-only baselines; kill the idea if it stays under 80% of full-mask PQ or within 1 PQ of point-loss baselines.
why_important: A validated 10-click protocol changes the economics of building new panoptic datasets and gives weak supervision a mechanism-level explanation of when clicks suffice.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Point-supervised segmentation exists (point-based training losses); the explicit topology-vs-geometry decomposition with click-pair affinity training and a percentage-of-full-PQ kill line appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Simulate click budgets on COCO panoptic, train a Mask2Former variant with click-pair affinity supervision on DINOv2 features vs point-loss baselines and full masks, and compare PQ at matched compute.
main_risk: Click simulation (uniform interior sampling) flatters the method relative to real annotator click distributions, which cluster near object centers and miss thin parts.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Weak supervision is expected to trade large accuracy losses for cost, and points are seen as too impoverished for panoptic-quality masks.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Affinity fields may fail exactly on the classes where masks matter most (articulated, thin, overlapping objects), leaving the gap concentrated and unacceptable.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Three trainings (affinity, point-loss, full) of Mask2Former-R50 on COCO panoptic subsets take about 3 days total on one A100; COCO and DINOv2 are public.

one_line_idea: Box-plus-one-interior-point supervision: adding a single interior click to each box annotation closes more than half of the box-only-to-full-mask instance segmentation gap by resolving the figure-ground ambiguity that box supervision cannot.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Box-supervised instance segmentation (BoxInst lineage) works surprisingly well but plateaus below full-mask training, and the annotation-cost ladder between boxes and masks has no validated intermediate rung.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The dominant failure of box-only training is figure-ground inversion inside the box (mask latches onto background or a co-occurring object), a single guaranteed-foreground point removes exactly this ambiguity, so its marginal value is far higher than its marginal cost of about one click.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On COCO, box-plus-one-point training will close at least 55% of the mask-AP gap between box-only and full-mask training at under 5% additional annotation time; kill the idea if the gap closure is below 30%, which would mean box-only failures are not point-addressable.
why_important: Defines a new, costed rung on the supervision ladder that dataset builders can adopt immediately, with a mechanism (figure-ground disambiguation) that predicts where it helps.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Points and boxes have each been used as weak supervision; the marginal-value analysis of exactly one interior point on top of boxes, with a gap-closure kill line, appears untested.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Train BoxInst-style models under box-only, box+1-point (simulated from GT interiors), and full-mask regimes on COCO, then stratify gains by figure-ground-confusion cases identified in the box-only error analysis.
main_risk: The single point may be redundant with pairwise color-affinity terms already used in box-supervised losses, yielding gains well under the predicted closure.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] The supervision ladder is assumed to jump from boxes to masks, with intermediate signals dismissed as engineering noise.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Box-only failures may be dominated by boundary imprecision rather than figure-ground inversion, which a single point does nothing to fix.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Three CondInst/BoxInst trainings on COCO with MMDetection (about 1 A100-day each) plus error stratification complete in about 3 single-GPU days; all public.

one_line_idea: Scribble supervision with a topology-preserving connectivity loss recovers thin-structure segmentation (poles, fences, sign posts) that standard scribble training loses, at unchanged cost on thick classes.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Scribble-supervised segmentation approaches full supervision on bulky classes but collapses on thin, elongated structures, whose continuity is exactly what pixel-wise losses fail to enforce from sparse scribbles.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Thin-class failure under scribbles is a connectivity problem, not a data-quantity problem: adding a differentiable connectivity/topology penalty that requires predicted thin-class components to connect scribble endpoints restores continuity, so most of the thin-class gap closes without any extra annotation.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On Cityscapes with simulated scribbles, adding the connectivity loss will recover at least 60% of the thin-class (pole, traffic sign pole, fence) IoU gap between scribble and full supervision while changing thick-class IoU by under 0.5; kill the idea if thin-class gap recovery is under 25% or thick classes degrade by over 1.0 IoU.
why_important: Thin structures carry outsized downstream importance (infrastructure inspection, driving) and are the acknowledged weak point of every cheap-supervision protocol; a targeted repair makes scribbles viable end-to-end.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Topology-aware losses exist for full supervision in specialized pipelines; coupling them to scribble endpoints as a weak-supervision repair with a gap-recovery kill line appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Generate skeleton-based scribbles for Cityscapes, train DeepLabv3+ with and without the connectivity penalty, and report per-class IoU deltas stratified by structure thinness.
main_risk: Differentiable topology penalties are computationally heavy and unstable at high resolution, and a proxy (e.g., skeleton-overlap loss) may weaken the mechanism claim.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Thin-class failure is filed under insufficient supervision, with the assumed fix being more or denser annotation rather than a structural loss.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Thin-class failure may be dominated by feature-resolution limits of the backbone, in which case no loss on top of the same features can restore continuity.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two DeepLabv3+ trainings on Cityscapes (MMSegmentation) plus scribble generation run in about 1.5 days on one A100; data and models public.

one_line_idea: SSL-native weak supervision: replacing CAM-style seeds with clustering of frozen self-supervised features as the seed generator lifts image-label-only segmentation by a measurable margin under an otherwise identical pipeline.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Image-label-only semantic segmentation pipelines still bootstrap from class activation maps, a mechanism designed for supervised classifiers a decade ago, while frozen self-supervised features now carry strong object geometry.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] CAM seeds are the binding constraint of weakly supervised pipelines (their errors propagate through refinement), and attention/feature clustering of a frozen SSL backbone produces seeds with strictly better boundary recall at matched precision, so swapping only the seed generator improves the whole pipeline without new hyperparameter tuning.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On Pascal VOC 2012 with an identical refinement and training stack, SSL-cluster seeds will improve final mIoU by at least 3.0 points over CAM seeds, and seed-quality metrics (boundary recall at matched precision) will improve by at least 10 points; kill the idea if final mIoU gains are at or under 1.0 point, meaning refinement already saturates seed quality.
why_important: Isolates and upgrades the weakest module of a widely used cheap-supervision recipe, and the seed-quality-to-final-quality transfer curve is itself a reusable diagnostic capability.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] SSL features have been used for unsupervised segmentation; a controlled seed-swap study inside a standard weakly supervised pipeline with a propagation analysis appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Hold refinement (CRF/affinity) and final training fixed on VOC; compare CAM, improved-CAM variants, and DINOv2-cluster seeds; regress final mIoU on seed quality across the variants.
main_risk: SSL clusters lack class labels, and the assignment of clusters to image-level labels may introduce a new error mode that cancels seed-quality gains.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Progress in weakly supervised segmentation is expected from better refinement and losses, with CAM seeding treated as a settled component.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Modern refinement stages may already correct most seed errors, making the pipeline insensitive to seed quality above a low floor.

one_line_idea: Complement-masked training for disjointly labeled dataset unions: masking the loss over classes a source did not label, plus cross-image class banks, trains one model from three partially labeled datasets to near fully-labeled-union quality.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Real datasets label different class subsets (driving sets lack indoor classes and vice versa), and naive union training punishes correct predictions of classes the current source treats as background.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] The union-training failure is a supervision-semantics bug, not a data limitation: treating unlabeled classes as ignore (complement masking) removes the false-negative gradients, and a class-bank memory that replays confident cross-dataset features restores the missing positive signal, together recovering nearly all of the fully-labeled-union performance.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Splitting ADE20K classes into three disjoint label groups across three sub-datasets, complement masking plus class banks will train a model within 2.0 mIoU of the fully-labeled-union reference, versus a naive-union baseline at least 8 mIoU below it; kill the idea if the method stays more than 5 mIoU below the reference, meaning partial labeling loses irrecoverable information.
why_important: A validated recipe for disjoint-label unions unlocks training on the union of existing public datasets without any re-annotation, one of the cheapest data-scaling moves available.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Partial-label semantics and cross-dataset training have been studied piecemeal; a controlled disjoint-split benchmark with a recovery-gap kill line appears missing.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Create the controlled three-way split of ADE20K, train naive-union, complement-masked, masked-plus-bank, and full-union references with SegFormer, and compare mIoU and per-group breakdowns.
main_risk: Class banks rely on confident pseudo-features whose errors could compound for visually similar cross-group classes, capping recovery below the target.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Practitioners assume datasets with different label spaces cannot be merged without relabeling or per-dataset heads.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Context co-occurrence across groups may be irreplaceable: without seeing labeled sofa and labeled wall in the same image, boundary calibration between them may never form.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Four SegFormer-B0 trainings on ADE20K splits take about 2 days total on one A100; ADE20K and SegFormer are public.

one_line_idea: A clicks-to-quality scaling law: interactive annotation quality follows a power law in click budget whose exponent is shared across datasets and interfaces, enabling annotation-budget planning from a 50-image pilot.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Annotation campaigns set click and time budgets by folklore, with no quantitative law connecting per-instance interaction budget to achieved label quality across datasets.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Achieved mask quality as a function of interaction budget follows a saturating power law whose exponent reflects boundary complexity statistics that are broadly shared across natural-image datasets, so a small pilot suffices to fit the curve and predict the budget needed for any target quality on a new dataset.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] Fitting the law on 50-image pilots from COCO and ADE20K (simulated interaction via public interactive-segmentation models) will predict the full clicks-to-IoU curve on Cityscapes and Pascal VOC within 5% quality error across budgets of 1-20 clicks; kill the idea if cross-dataset prediction error exceeds 15% or if fitted exponents differ across datasets by more than a factor of 2, breaking the shared-exponent claim.
why_important: Turns annotation budgeting into measurement: a lab can decide clicks-per-instance and campaign cost from a one-afternoon pilot instead of guesswork.

main_risk: Simulated clicking underestimates human variability, so the law may hold for robot users but fail for real annotator populations.

one_line_idea: Train-time depth as free boundary supervision: distilling depth-discontinuity and normal-discontinuity maps from RGB-D training data into a 2D segmentation model improves boundary quality with zero test-time depth requirement.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Public RGB-D datasets carry precise geometric discontinuities that align with object boundaries, yet 2D segmentation training typically ignores the depth channel even when it is available at training time.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Boundary supervision is the scarcest part of the segmentation signal, and depth/normal discontinuities provide a dense, annotation-free boundary teacher; an auxiliary boundary-distillation loss from train-time depth therefore improves boundary-F on RGB-only inference more than equivalent-compute image-only auxiliary losses.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On NYUv2 (RGB-only at test), depth-discontinuity distillation will improve boundary-F by at least 3.0 points and mIoU by at least 1.0 over the no-auxiliary baseline, and by at least 1.5 boundary-F over an edge-detector-distillation control at matched compute; kill the idea if it fails to beat the edge-distillation control by 0.5 boundary-F, meaning geometry adds nothing beyond photometric edges.
why_important: Recasts existing RGB-D archives as free supervision for ordinary 2D models, a capability claim about supervision sources rather than architectures, with a control that isolates the geometric contribution.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Depth-aware segmentation typically consumes depth at test time; train-only geometric-boundary distillation with a photometric-edge control appears under-examined.

one_line_idea: Learned exclusion-composition matrices for panoptic decoding: a soft constraint matrix over class pairs (mutual exclusion, adjacency plausibility) applied during mask assembly reduces stuff-thing confusion errors at equal PQ elsewhere.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Panoptic outputs contain characteristic label-composition errors (sea pixels inside vehicle masks, sky patches under bridges labeled as building) that per-mask confidences do not police.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Class-pair composition statistics (which labels legitimately touch or nest) are stable, learnable priors whose enforcement at mask-assembly time corrects composition errors that arise from mask-level independence assumptions in query-based decoders.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On COCO panoptic, constraint-matrix assembly will reduce composition-violation pixels (label adjacencies absent from training statistics) by at least 40% and improve PQ-stuff by at least 0.8 with PQ-things within 0.3, versus the unconstrained decoder; kill the idea if PQ-stuff gains are under 0.2, meaning composition errors are cosmetically rare or self-correcting.
why_important: Moves scene-level coherence from hope to mechanism in panoptic decoding, with a constraint component reusable across query-based architectures.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Pairwise label compatibility was central to CRF-era segmentation; reviving it as a learned assembly-stage constraint for query-based panoptic decoders with a violation-rate kill line appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Estimate composition statistics from COCO panoptic training data, integrate the soft constraint into Mask2Former's assembly step, and compare violation rates, PQ splits, and per-class deltas against the unconstrained baseline.
main_risk: Global statistics may suppress rare-but-valid compositions (boats on land in shipyards), trading visible errors for invisible ones on unusual scenes.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Query-based decoders are assumed to have made pairwise label priors obsolete; composition errors are tolerated as residual noise.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Composition violations may co-occur with mask-boundary errors that the constraint cannot fix, so violations drop without any PQ movement.
fastest_falsification_experiment: One Mask2Former panoptic finetune with the constraint layer on COCO takes about 1.5 days on one A100; all data and baselines public.

one_line_idea: Reflection-equivariant heads for man-made categories: enforcing horizontal-mirror equivariance in the decoder improves boundary quality on bilaterally symmetric classes without degrading asymmetric ones, isolating symmetry as an exploitable output prior.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] Many man-made and biological categories are bilaterally symmetric, yet segmentation decoders learn left and right boundary evidence independently and show asymmetric error patterns on symmetric objects.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Symmetry is a per-category structural prior that decoders fail to exploit from data alone; an equivariant head that shares computation across the estimated symmetry axis pools boundary evidence from both sides, improving symmetric-class boundaries specifically, with the class-stratified contrast isolating the mechanism.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On ADE20K and PACO symmetric classes (vehicles, furniture, containers), the equivariant head will improve boundary-F by at least 2.0 points while asymmetric-class boundary-F stays within 0.5, and gains will correlate with per-instance symmetry scores (rho at least 0.4); kill the idea if symmetric-class gains are under 0.7 or asymmetric classes degrade by over 1.0.
why_important: Demonstrates a reusable route for injecting object-level structural priors into dense decoders, with the symmetric/asymmetric contrast as a built-in control that most architecture papers lack.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Equivariant networks target global transformations; per-instance estimated-axis symmetry exploitation in dense decoding with a class-stratified kill test appears new.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Add a symmetry-axis estimator and mirror-shared decoding path to a Mask2Former head, train matched pairs on ADE20K/PACO, and evaluate class-stratified boundary-F with the symmetry-score correlation analysis.
main_risk: Axis estimation errors on occluded or perspective-distorted instances could inject wrong-side evidence, hurting exactly the difficult cases.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Symmetry is assumed to be learned implicitly from data when useful, making architectural enforcement unnecessary.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Perspective projection breaks image-plane symmetry for most 3D-symmetric objects, so the exploitable prior may be too weak outside frontal views.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Two head trainings on frozen DINOv2 features for ADE20K/PACO subsets take about 1 day on one consumer GPU; all data and backbones public.

one_line_idea: Kinematic-manifold projection for 2D pose: projecting keypoint predictions onto a learned manifold of anthropometrically valid poses at decode time eliminates impossible outputs and improves occluded-joint accuracy on frozen pose models.
problem: [KNOWN FACT] 2D pose estimators emit anatomically impossible configurations (impossible joint angles, incompatible bone-length ratios) under occlusion, because per-joint heatmaps are decoded independently.
core_hypothesis: [HYPOTHESIS] Valid 2D projections of human poses occupy a low-dimensional manifold learnable from pose data alone; decoding by projecting heatmap evidence onto this manifold replaces impossible configurations with the nearest valid ones, improving occluded joints (where evidence is weak and the prior should dominate) while leaving visible joints untouched.
falsifiable_prediction: [EXPECTED RESULT] On COCO keypoints with a frozen public ViTPose model, manifold projection will improve PCK on occlusion-flagged joints by at least 2.0 points with visible-joint PCK within 0.3, and reduce impossible-configuration outputs (violating joint-angle/bone-ratio limits) by at least 70%; kill the idea if occluded-joint gains are under 0.7 points, meaning heatmap ambiguity is not prior-recoverable.
why_important: Guaranteed-valid pose outputs matter for downstream biomechanics and animation consumers, and the decode-time design upgrades deployed models without retraining.
why_possibly_novel: [MODEL SPECULATION / unverified] Pose priors and manifold models are classical; a frozen-model decode-time projection with occlusion-stratified kill thresholds and validity guarantees appears untested on modern pose stacks.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Learn the valid-pose manifold (VAE or normalizing flow on COCO keypoint annotations), implement projection decoding over frozen ViTPose heatmaps, and evaluate occlusion-stratified PCK plus validity-violation rates against soft-prior baselines.
main_risk: The manifold learned from annotated (mostly visible) poses may not cover extreme-but-valid athletic configurations, suppressing correct rare predictions.
community_default_belief: [MODEL SPECULATION] Modern heatmap models are assumed to have internalized pose priors, making explicit structural decoding redundant.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Errors under occlusion may be spatially large but manifold-consistent (wrong but valid poses), which projection cannot detect or fix.
fastest_falsification_experiment: Manifold training on COCO keypoint annotations plus decode-time evaluation with the public ViTPose checkpoint runs in under 1 day on one consumer GPU; all public.
